A local disk of 14 faces, redrawn with equal-sided triangles. Drag to see the folds, or flatten for a clear overhead map. The rest of the surface is omitted.

Click two numbered vertices, or use the selectors. Blue and orange show the completing triangles; gold marks their shared edge. Use 2× or 4× and scroll to follow a route.

What do the two answers mean?

Blue marks a dark face of the original PG(3,2): the third label is A XOR B. Orange marks a light face of the second Steiner triple system. The gold curve is the shared edge A–B. Every distinct pair has exactly one answer in each system.

The neighborhood preserves the cyclic order and labels of all 14 incident faces. At full fold its triangles are equilateral; flattening changes lengths but not connections. This is a local re-embedding, not an isometric piece of the necklace. The whole-surface view stretches the original surface vertically, preserving genus, all faces, and all curved-edge connections. Thickness does not redistribute the edges around vertices. Hover a face for its oriented triple.
